lines.text: In 2007, Warren Buffett bet a million dollars that the laziest portfolio on Earth would beat Wall Street's smartest money.
lines.say: In two thousand seven, Warren Buffett bet a million dollars that the laziest portfolio on Earth would beat Wall Street's smartest money.

lines.text: His pick: a plain S&P 500 index fund. Own everything. Pay almost nothing.
lines.say: His pick: a plain S and P five hundred index fund. Own everything. Pay almost nothing.

lines.text: Against him: Ted Seides of Protégé Partners, with five funds of hedge funds.
lines.say: Against him: Ted Seides of Protégé Partners, with five funds of hedge funds.

lines.text: Ten years. 2008 to 2017. Scored after every fee.
lines.say: Ten years. Two thousand eight to twenty seventeen. Scored after every fee.

lines.text: Buffett wasn't forecasting the market. His logic was arithmetic.
Before costs, active managers as a group earn the market's return, because together, they are the market.
After costs, they must trail it. And hedge funds charge in layers: 2% a year, plus 20% of gains, then another layer on top.
lines.say: After costs, they must trail it. And hedge funds charge in layers: two percent a year, plus twenty percent of gains, then another layer on top.

lines.text: Skill was uncertain. Costs were certain.
Then came year one. In 2008, the market fell 37%. The hedge funds lost less. Buffett was behind.
lines.say: Then came year one. In two thousand eight, the market fell thirty-seven percent. The hedge funds lost less. Buffett was behind.

lines.text: He didn't move. A ten-year bet is scored at year ten.
Even the stake held a lesson. It sat in Treasury bonds, set to be worth a million dollars in 2017.
lines.say: Even the stake held a lesson. It sat in Treasury bonds, set to be worth a million dollars in twenty seventeen.

lines.text: By 2012, those safe bonds would pay under 1% a year. So both sides moved the stake into Berkshire stock.
lines.say: By twenty twelve, those safe bonds would pay under one percent a year. So both sides moved the stake into Berkshire stock.

lines.text: Risk isn't a price that wiggles. It's the chance you miss your goal.
December 2017. The index fund: up 126%, about 8.5% a year.
lines.say: December, twenty seventeen. The index fund: up a hundred and twenty-six percent, about eight and a half percent a year.

lines.text: The five funds of funds: between 3% and 88%. Every one trailed.
lines.say: The five funds of funds: between three and eighty-eight percent. Every one trailed.

lines.text: By Buffett's estimate, roughly 60% of their gains had gone to the managers.
lines.say: By Buffett's estimate, roughly sixty percent of their gains had gone to the managers.

lines.text: Seides made a fair point: a roaring bull market favored the index. One decade is one sample.
But the arithmetic of costs holds in any decade.
Performance comes, performance goes. Fees never falter.
If you can't know who will win, own the whole field, and keep what it earns.
